newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-SCALA IN TALKS WITH JAPANESE AND GERMAN CLUBS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SCALA IN TALKS WITH JAPANESE AND GERMAN CLUBS.

text.p: Former Parma coach Nevio Scala has been talking to Japanese and German clubs, Gazzetta dello Sport reported on Thursday.
Scala, who has been suggested as an outside candidate for the vacant job of Italy coach, was evaluating a lucrative offer from an unidentified club in Japan, the newspaper said.
It said Scala had discussions with Japanese officials at his home on Wednesday and had been invited to visit Japan next week to assess the situation.
But the newspaper also quoted Scala as saying that he had spoken to former German international Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, Bayern Munich's vice-chairman.

"I have spoken to Rummenigge, in the space of a few days in Germany there could be a lot of new things in various clubs. There could be some good opportunities there as well. And I have an obligation to evaluate all the offers I get," he said.
Bayern coach Giovanni Trapattoni has headed opinion polls in Italy as the man most people want to take the Italy job following Arrigo Sacchi's resignation.
Under-21 coach Cesare Maldini is generally regarded as having the job sewn up but possibly only for a limited period.

Corriere dello Sport reported on Thursday that the Italian soccer federation wanted Trapattoni and said the former Juventus and Internazionale coach had signalled he was willing to take the helm once the German season had finished.
It said Maldini would be confirmed until the summer of 1997 when Italy's performance under him would be assessed.

Scala, who coached Parma to the UEFA and European Cup Winners' Cups, said on Tuesday that he could soon be coaching a foreign team. "It will not be Barcelona or Borussia Moenchengladbach," he added, naming no other clubs.
